docRequirement: `whats-new/2026-w13.md:154` binds us to an agent-definition frontmatter field named exactly `initialPrompt`: "Agents can declare initialPrompt in frontmatter to auto-submit a first turn". `sub-agents.md:293` gives its full contract and its precondition: "Auto-submitted as the first user turn when this agent runs as the main session agent (via `--agent` or the `agent` setting). Commands and skills are processed. Prepended to any user-provided prompt" — so the binding is three things at once: the field is parsed and carried on a definition, a main-session-agent surface exists (`--agent ` flag, the `agent` key in settings, or the `--agents` JSON flag which lists `initialPrompt` among its accepted fields at `sub-agents.md:223`), and when such a session starts the value is submitted as the first user turn, prepended to any prompt the user supplied.
current: The identifier does not exist anywhere in the product: `grep -rani initialprompt packages apps scripts` (broad, `-a`, no `--include` filter so NUL-byte files are not skipped) returns 0 hits; the only repo occurrences are prose in `docs/`. All three definition paths omit it. (1) The markdown/JSON loader: `AgentDefinition` at packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:58-122 carries `model`, `disallowedTools`, `maxTurns`, `permissionMode`, `effort`, `memory`, `background`, `color`, `isolation`, `skillKeys`, `mcpServerKeys` and no `initialPrompt`; the input shape `UserAgentDefinition` at :254-272 lists the same 16 keys without it; `normalizeUserAgentDefinition` at :383-460 has no read and no reject-on-malformed clause for it (contrast :433 for `color`). (2) The capability/plugin path: the wire descriptor `PiRuntimeAgentDefinitionDescriptor` at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:121-145 has no such member, `buildPiRuntimeAgentDescriptor` at :546-640 never reads it out of the frontmatter record, and `parseDefinitionEntry` at :286-382 never validates it. (3) Unknown frontmatter keys are silently dropped, not diagnosed: `parseFrontmatter` (definitions.ts:490-519) and `splitMarkdownFrontmatter` (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/shared.ts:275-320) collect every key into a record and the readers pick only named fields, so an `initialPrompt:` line produces no error, no warning and no doctor diagnostic. Recorded as a costed deviation at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-subagent-frontmatter.md:150 and harvested to docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:309.
divergence: Not a key-name or value-shape mismatch — nothing of this mechanism exists. The delta is two-layered and the second layer is why the first alone is not a fix. (a) The field: `initialPrompt` is absent from the definition type, from both frontmatter readers, from the Pi wire descriptor and from both strict validators, and an author's `initialPrompt:` line is discarded without a diagnostic. (b) The scope the doc gives the field: no way exists to run an agent definition as the main session — no `--agent`/`--agents` flag, no `agent` setting, no agent field on `CreateSessionOptions` — so even a correctly parsed value would have no moment at which the doc says to submit it, and per this repo's inert-contract rule it would be a parsed-but-unconsumed key. Also unimplemented, and easy to miss when scoping: the `Prepended to any user-provided prompt` rule (`sub-agents.md:293`) is composition, not replacement — the first turn is `initialPrompt` + the user's prompt, with commands and skills processed in it.

change.what: Add `initialPrompt?: string` to `AgentDefinition` (:58-122) and `initialPrompt?: unknown` to `UserAgentDefinition` (:254-272). Add a `normalizeInitialPrompt(value)` beside `normalizeColor` (:377) that requires a string, trims, rejects empty and caps length; wire it in `normalizeUserAgentDefinition` (:383-460) with the established reject-on-malformed clause (copy the `entry.color !== undefined && color === undefined` shape at :433) and spread it into the returned object at :456-459. Do NOT add the key to `ARRAY_FRONTMATTER_KEYS` (:279) — it is a scalar, and listing it would split a prompt containing commas into a list. `parseFrontmatter` (:490-519) has no YAML block-scalar support: `initialPrompt: |` matches the scalar regex at :498 and stores the literal string "|", so either teach it `|`/`>` blocks or make `normalizeInitialPrompt` reject a bare `|`/`>` value rather than submit it as a turn.

Add `initialPrompt?: string` to the descriptor (:121-145) and a `MAX_AGENT_INITIAL_PROMPT_LENGTH` beside the other bounds (:19-24). In `parseDefinitionEntry` (:286-382) validate it with `boundedString` and include it in the `parsed` object (:352-375) — it must be inside the object hashed at :376-379, or the digest check rejects every descriptor that carries it. Decide explicitly whether the key joins `PLUGIN_IGNORED_AGENT_FRONTMATTER` (:399-431): the docs' ignored-for-plugin trio is `hooks`/`mcpServers`/`permissionMode` only, so the doc-faithful answer is that it is allowed, but a plugin-supplied main-session agent that auto-submits its own first turn is a trust decision that should be recorded either way.

blastRadius: Crosses both a wire boundary and a persistence boundary, so this is a risk trigger by this repo's rule. (1) IPC/wire: `PiRuntimeAgentDefinitionDescriptor` is sent to the Pi subprocess and re-parsed there — packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:2749 calls `parsePiRuntimeAgentDefinitions`, and the descriptor is content-addressed (`definitionDigest` built at runtime-agent-definition.ts:231-233, verified at :376-379). A field added on the host but not inside the hashed object, or a host/subprocess pair built from different sources, makes every definition fail the digest check and vanish from the session. `materializePiRuntimeAgentDefinitions` has 7 callers in SessionManager and covering tests in runtime-agent-definition.test.ts, pi-runtime-agent-definition.test.ts and SessionManager.orchestration.test.ts. (2) Protocol: `CreateSessionOptions` is consumed by apps/cli (`sessions:create` at apps/cli/src/index.ts:392, :841, :1339, :1428), by the electron main process and by server-core; adding a field is additive but every producer needs the new value threaded. (3) Persistence: the main-session agent choice must survive resume, which puts it in the session record — a migration-shaped change. (4) Diagnostics: both strict validators (`validateMarkdownAgentDefinitionContent`, definitions.ts:620; `validatePiRuntimeAgentDefinitionContent`, runtime-agent-definition.ts:512) feed the `nessy-general-agent doctor` surface, so a new reject path changes doctor output. (5) Imported-plugin path: plugin-bundled agent files flow through the same `buildPiRuntimeAgentDescriptor`, and `withPluginExclusions` (:423-431) is the trust gate that decides whether a plugin may set this field. (6) User-facing docs: the agent frontmatter table in docs-site en+ru.
userImpact: None observable today, in either direction. A user cannot express the intent — there is no `--agent` flag, no `--agents` flag and no `agent` setting, so no agent definition ever runs as the main session and there is no turn for an `initialPrompt` to be submitted into. And a user who writes `initialPrompt:` in `~/.nessy-agent/agents/<name>.md`, or installs a Claude plugin whose agent file carries it, sees nothing at all: the key is silently discarded by both frontmatter readers, the agent still loads and runs normally, and no error, warning or doctor line names the ignored field. It surfaces the moment a main-session-agent surface ships (the field would then be the only part still missing), or as a support question the first time someone ports a Claude agent that relies on the auto-submitted turn and gets an empty session instead — with nothing on screen to explain why.
